The most common win left on "Ravens X10" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $50,000, and two of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Tomorrow's count on "Ravens X10" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
808.headline: What's actually left to win

809.body:
About a third of the tickets for "Gold Bar Bingo" have been sold. The game is about halfway through its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

Everything here about "Gold Bar Bingo" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through November 26.
809.headline: Where this game is in its run

810.body:
One of In the Green's top prizes was claimed in this morning's update. A player in Maryland won $50,000. The game started with seven top prizes and now has three top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

Every line of In the Green's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
810.headline: Another top prize was claimed

811.body:
The key fact about "Extreme Green" is how its eleven prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward small, frequent prizes. Games built like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

Every line of Extreme Green's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
811.headline: How the prize money is divided

812.body:
On "Loose Change®", one $1,000 top prize was claimed yesterday. That leaves fourteen of the original 24. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Everything above about "Loose Change®" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.

"Deluxe Crossword" is down to five top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed in this morning's update. The game started with eight top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

The numbers for "Deluxe Crossword" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
816.headline: A top prize was just claimed

"Hello Money!" is down to four top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed over a week ago. The game started with seven top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

Tomorrow's count on "Hello Money!" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.

818.headline: What's actually left to win

"30X Cash" has 229,684 prizes of $30 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $5,000 prize, with 35 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If you play "30X Cash" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
819.headline: The prize table, line by line

820.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Cozy Cash", about three-quarters are still unsold. The game is still new, with 32 of 35 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

The numbers for "Cozy Cash" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
820.headline: Early stage or late

821.body:
A $10,000 top prize on "Season's Greetings" was claimed in today's numbers. The game started with six top prizes and has four top prizes left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

Everything above about "Season's Greetings" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
821.headline: Top prize count went down

822.body:
The top prize count on "Peppermint Payout" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has six of six top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Everything above about "Peppermint Payout" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
822.headline: No top prize claimed lately

823.body:
About a quarter of the tickets for "Holly-Day Cash" have been sold. The game is near the midpoint of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

Everything here about "Holly-Day Cash" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through November 26.
823.headline: Where this game is in its run

824.body:
"Winter Multiplier" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $100,000 was claimed yesterday. Unsold tickets still hold seven of the original nine. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

Today's free summary of "Winter Multiplier" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
824.headline: A player won a top prize

825.body:
"Win $100, $200 or $500" has 11,284 of 12,822 top prizes left and is early in its run. About a quarter of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

Everything here about "Win $100, $200 or $500" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through November 26.

"White Elephant" has joined the Maryland lineup at $1 with twenty top prizes of $500. Only on the first day do the overall odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.
